title: Secure file transfer software compared
content_html:
There is no single best secure file transfer tool; you need to evaluate based on your requirements. A useful secure file transfer software comparison starts with your own needs, not with a ranking. Check who can open a file and how you remove that access. Check where files are stored and what the vendor's terms say about your data. Check whether the tool links to the systems your team already uses. Then compare each tool against those points.

Features and terms change, so the only reliable source for any tool is its own website and terms, read on the day you decide. What follows is the method, the main kinds of option, competitor tools, and an honest note on where Upward Technologies (upwardtech.nl) fits.

Secure file transfer software comparison: the tools and their strengths

Here is how popular secure file transfer tools and methods compare against key evaluation criteria.

Tool / MethodStrengthsBest For
Microsoft OneDrive / SharePointIntegrated into existing Microsoft 365 ecosystems, robust enterprise permission controls, and familiar user interface.Teams heavily invested in the Microsoft ecosystem sharing internal or moderately sensitive files.
Google DriveSeamless collaboration, ubiquitous user adoption, and easy link sharing with granular view/edit rights.Fast-paced teams already using Google Workspace who need simple cloud storage and sharing.
WeTransferExtremely fast and frictionless for large files without requiring an account for the sender or recipient.Quick, ad-hoc transfers of large media files where long-term retention or granular access control is not required.
KiteworksHigh-level compliance focus (FedRAMP, HIPAA), advanced governance, and rigorous tracking of all file movements.Regulated industries (healthcare, finance, government) with strict data residency and security mandates.
Transfer by Upward TechnologiesStandalone simplicity at transfer.upwardtech.nl with no custom software required, backed by custom integration options.Businesses seeking a straightforward Dutch-hosted alternative or custom-tailored file workflows.

Secure file transfer software comparison: the questions that separate tools

Ask every tool on your shortlist the same questions. Write the answers down from the vendor's own pages, not from memory or a review site.

QuestionWhy it matters
Who can open a file once it is sent?This decides whether a forwarded link or email also forwards access.
Can you remove access after sending?Files sent by mistake need a way back.
Where are files stored, and for how long?Your own policy or your clients' contracts may set rules on this.
What do the vendor's terms say about your data?Read the terms yourself and do not rely on marketing pages.
Is there a processing agreement for personal data?If files hold personal data, you will need one with the vendor.
Can you see who sent and opened what?A record helps when a client or auditor asks.
Does it connect to the systems you already use?Without this, people download and upload the same files by hand.
Who supports it when something breaks?You need a named contact, not a guess.

The main kinds of option

Email attachments

Most teams start here because everyone already has email. Whether it is enough depends on how sensitive the files are and what your own policy says. The reasons many businesses move away from it are covered in why email attachments and shared links fall short for secure file transfer.

Shared links from file storage

Many teams already pay for file storage that can share a link to a file or folder. This can be a good fit when the files are not very sensitive and the people receiving them are known. Check the vendor's terms on how stored files and links are handled before you use it for client or personal data.

Dedicated secure file transfer tools

These are products built mainly for sending files to people outside the company. They suit teams that send files to many different recipients and want one tool for it. Compare them using the table above, and read each vendor's own pages and terms.

Client portals

When the same clients send and receive files again and again, a portal gives them one place to log in and find everything. This fits accountants, advisers and service firms with long-running client relationships. The trade-offs between buying a portal and having one built are in client portal development: when to build custom vs buy off-the-shelf.

How we compared

  • Same questions for every option. The questions above are the test, applied to every kind of option equally.
  • Vendor sources only. Any claim about a tool should come from its own website and terms, with the date you read them.
  • Fit over features. The right answer depends on who you send files to, how often, and what your policy requires.

FAQ

Which secure file transfer software is best?

There is no single best secure file transfer tool; you need to evaluate based on your requirements, such as compliance needs, ease of use, and integration capabilities.

Are email attachments secure enough for business files?

For highly sensitive or personal data, email attachments usually fall short because they lack access revocation, audit trails, and encryption-at-rest guarantees.

Do I need a custom client portal or an off-the-shelf tool?

Off-the-shelf tools suit general ad-hoc sharing, whereas custom client portals fit service firms and accountants with long-running, repeating client relationships.
